creativePromise: An overlooked child and a slow, warm panda build a walking cardboard rover, turn playground obstacles into a shared expedition, and bring the original group along.
hiddenUnderlayer: Joining need not mean winning the existing role; making space and sharing control creates a reciprocal friendship.
openingHook: The child brings a handmade steering wheel, but the pretend station already has a driver and nobody hears the invitation.
childWant: To drive, contribute something personal, and be heard by the other children.
physicalProblem: An occupied station, a sandbox to go around, pretend lava across grass, a curling rug and a bench obstruct the route.
playRule: Ordinary playground materials become pretend space equipment, but move only through ordinary bodily actions.

setPieces.name: Sandbox and yellow flower
setPieces.dramaticUse: A telescope reframes a nearby flower as a shared destination.

setPieces.name: Rolled play rug
setPieces.dramaticUse: A comic failed unrolling becomes a cooperative route.

setPieces.name: Bench and bush
setPieces.dramaticUse: Narrow telescope vision yields to a wider view and a child-led detour.

lockedCausalMovement: The ignored steering wheel leads the child to Adam and the telescope.
The telescope reveals a flower, prompting construction of the bottomless walking box.
The child returns to invite the station group rather than leaving them behind.
The pretend lava rule leads to the rug; the companion's soft tumble leads to cooperative flattening.
Sharing driving lets the child navigate; lowering the telescope reveals the bench detour.
Adam yields the wheel as agreed; the group returns and finally gives the companion time to speak.
companionWrongHelp: Waiting for the perfect pause initially allows the game to restart; later the slow turn and curling rug create gentle physical comedy.

The companion sits on a curling rug edge.
comicEscalations.consequence: The road seems to try travelling on its own.

comicEscalations.setup: Everyone waits for the companion's final suggestion.
comicEscalations.consequence: The road, not the companion, supposedly needs a seat.

attempts.attempt: Offer the wheel at the occupied entrance.
attempts.failure: Pretend engine noises drown out the child.

attempts.attempt: Invite the group across the lawn.
attempts.failure: Their new pretend lava rule requires a different route.
The bench blocks the narrow view until the child lowers the tube.

childDiscovery: A new route and shared roles invite others in; looking beyond a narrow view reveals room to move.
childClimaxAction: The child lowers the telescope, finds the side path, directs the detour and later leads the return.
visiblePayoff: The group reaches the flower, Adam keeps the turn-taking promise, and the return call gets answers.
endingEnergy: A warm group conversation after packing up, ending on the road-needs-a-seat joke.
rereadHooks: The little flower is visible before becoming the destination.
The slow companion notices what the fast game misses.
The travelling-road joke returns at the end.

lineTargets.parentReread: בשביל הדרך. היא נסעה היום המון.

companionIndispensability: The companion notices Adam, helps support the walking box, causes the rug gag, points to the telescope during the role dispute and stops the box safely before the bench; the child supplies the route and invitation.
worldAndSafetyLocks: One enclosed, supervised playground in daylight.
Space, crater, sun and lava are pretend labels; no real rocket, lava or alien landscape.
Lightweight bottomless box moved by feet, no motor or actual wheels.
Rug lies on clear level ground; soft seated landing, no fall from height.
Flower and ladybug are observed without touching.
mustAvoid: Companion solving the detour instead of the child
Permanent exclusion or ridicule by the group
Duplicate limbs or multiple moments combined into one body
Inheriting visual directions from the predecessor story
oldStoryAntiCopy: Use only revision02 as the page sequence; the predecessor is lineage evidence, not a source of visual directions.
modelFreedom: Minor environmental texture and expressive staging within the source actions.
Camera position within the fresh directions; no changes to prose, roles or physical sequence.
